packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-03 -- isolated first reading (unverified image reading)
No identification of the work or author was revealed in my context. I did nothing beyond the rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001)
image-001: one plate with three separate paper fragments on black, colour checker lower left, ruler at right.
 Fragment A (centre-left, portrait): German cursive (Kurrent), single column, c. 30 lines, many lines struck through
   with horizontal strokes (cancelled draft), interlinear additions above lines. Pencil shelfmark at lower left
   ("Stams, Stb. Fragm. 183 2a"?) and a circled "3" (?) at foot; at foot a line in larger different script "Et porta infer..."(?).
   Edges cropped: line beginnings on left margin and ends on right are cut.
 Fragment B (upper right, roughly square, damaged with holes and torn lower/left edges): Latin, single column,
   ruled vertical line at left (text begins just right of it); faded brownish ink; short entries each beginning
   with a term ("Definitio ...", "Quaestio ...", "Libertas ...", "Translatio ..." etc.) -- tentatively a list
   of definitions. Pencil shelfmark along left edge, vertical: "Stams, Stb. Fragm. 183 1a"(?).
 Fragment C (lower right, landscape): Latin cursive, single column, c. 13 lines, left edge cropped (line beginnings lost);
   a grey card covers the right portion of the image area (masking? or a label) beside its lower right.
 Overview images 011 and 021 cover further faces (presumably the other sides); surveyed below when reached.
Tile mapping assumption: 002-010 are a 3x3 grid over image-001 (002-004 top row, 005-007 middle, 008-010 bottom;
 left column 002/005/008 lies over black background and colour checker -- not opened, as fragments lie in middle/right columns).

=== image-004 (top-right tile of plate 001): Fragment B, upper part ===
Observation: pale brown ink, single column; a vertical ruled line runs down near the right edge of the paper (text runs up to/over it);
headings centred ("De quaestione", "Metaphora ex Virgilio"); entries start with an enlarged first letter. Hole in centre.
Left edge of this tile may cut the first letters of some lines (see 003 overlap). A faint horizontal line runs under "enunciati..".
004.1  Definitio nominis est, quando aspicimus rem ipsam nom[cut?]
004.2  ppiam(? = propriam, start cut) et definimus ipsum, ut rethorica, quae constat
004.3  decem literis.          [first letters may be cut at left: "..decem"?]
004.4                (centred) De quaestione
004.5  Quaestio est in dubitationem ambiguitate(m)? adducta? [last word faint: "adducta"/"addicta"?]
004.6  enunciatio? [ending looks "-atibe"/"-atio"; uncertain]
004.7                (centred, first letters struck or blotted) Metaphora ex Virgilio
004.8  Libertas quae sera tame(n) respexit inertem
004.9  Translatio ab eo qui miser[hole]? respicit.
004.10 quente?, Metaphora, qui de[hole/illegible] proprie? significatione?(m) [last word very faint: "significationem"?]
004.11 qui carent arte? ingeniis, inertes dicuntur.   [after "carent": "art[e]?" + "-tq-"? uncertain]
004.12 Tityre t[u]? pa[illegible] recubans sub tegmine fa[illegible]   [faint]
004.13 Exordium quod captat benevolentiam? a persona   ["benevolentiam" faint]
004.14 Tityri et simul eu(m)? felicem praedicat.        [right margin beside this line: "3o"/"30" in darker ink]
004.15 [illegible faint line, cut at bottom of tile]

=== image-003 (top-middle tile of plate 001) ===
CORRECTION to tile-mapping assumption: tiles are at ~3.5x overview scale and cover only the right part of the plate;
 002/005/008 cover Fragment A (German), 003/006/009 its right edge + left part of B/C, 004/007/010 the rest of B/C.
Shows left blank margin of Fragment B with vertical ruled line, and pencil shelfmark written vertically: "Stams, StA, Fag. 183_1r"? (modern).
Line beginnings of Fragment B confirmed complete (overlaps 004 lines 1-14):
003 = 004.1 "Definitio nomin.."; 004.2 begins "ipsam?" (read "ippiam/ipsiam") et defi..; 004.3 "decem literis."
 004.5 "Quaestio est"; 004.6 "enunciatio?"; 004.8 "Libertas"; 004.9 "Translatio"; 004.10 begins "quente," (so first word is
 complete as "quente"/"gnente"? -- uncertain); 004.11 "qui carent"; 004.12 "Tityre"; 004.13 "Exordium"; 004.14 "Tityri et".
A short horizontal rule is visible under "enunciati.." (= 004.6), spanning from the left ruling.
Lower-left corner of tile: right edge of Fragment A (German) line-ends: "..ommen"? / "..den Ale.."(struck?) / "..ist & Si.."/ "..samlet"? -- read on 002/006.

=== image-002 (top-left tile of plate 001): top of Fragment A (German, Kurrent) ===
Only the top c. 4 lines of A are in this tile (rest black). Left edge of A cuts first letters of each line.
Struck-through words marked {struck: ...}. A pale stain/abrasion in mid-line 2-3.
002.1  [..]bracht h(?)z Eva durch ihr sünd hoffart(?) und genommen   ["hoffart": "ho" + ligature, uncertain]
002.2  [..]il dem nipp?/neyd? des {struck: [illegible]} [stain] ... {struck?: Maria hat den Ale[..]}  [a stroke runs through "Maria hat den Ale.."; interlinear above it: [illegible]]
002.3  {struck: [..]deckt?} / {struck: das [illegible]}  [stain] ... Gott widerstrebt?/widersteht? d(en) Ho[ffärtigen?]  ["Ho.." cut at right edge of tile]
002.4  [cut at bottom of tile] ... Das hat ... [illegible] und sie samlet?  (continued on 005)

=== image-005 (middle-left tile of plate 001): Fragment A, lines 1-22 of the tile ===
Overlap: 005.1-4 = 002.1-4. Left edge of A cuts 1-3 letters of each line; right edge cuts line-ends (continued in 006?).
Hand: German Kurrent, 17th-c.-looking cursive (observation only), fast draft with many cancellations; Latin words in
a more upright Latin-style script ("virum", "sub potenti manu", "nisi effi.."). Interlinear additions written small above lines.
Many readings below are tentative; "?" after a word = uncertain.
005.1  [..]bracht h(?)z Eva durch ihr sünd hoffart und genommen
005.2  [..]il dem nipp?/neid? des {struck: [illegible]} [stain] .. {struck: Maria hat den Ale[..]}
005.3  {struck: [..]deckt?} , {struck: das [illegible]} [stain] Gott widerstrebt? d(en) Ho[..]
005.4  [..]bt er gnad. Und hat [stain] ge?erbt?/verdirbt? und sie samblt?/sanft?   [middle uncertain]
005.5  [Pa]radeis? verschlossen, Maria hat es eröffnet mit d[..]
005.6  [..]ng aus dem nipp?/neid? des mans, (interlinear above: "als"?) Maria {struck: die} Jungfr[au]
005.7  [..]ein Mann Christus? d(er) sohn Gottes, nach dem {struck: Proph[..]}   (interlinear above "nach dem": "wie man ...(?) ..." [illegible])
005.8  (left, small interlinear/marginal: "[..] durch? d(en) Prophet") [circum]dabit? virum {struck: d[..]} ein weib wird einen mann um[..]
005.9  [..]ngt die {struck: [illegible]} Mutter alle tugenten, die Wim[..]? 
005.10 {struck: [..] gleichsam Christus}, da er sagt          [gap]   {struck?: nisi effi[..]}
005.11 {struck?: [..]er die kleine kind so ..(?) ihr nit eingeh(en) in d(as) Reich}  [whole line under a long stroke? uncertain]
005.12 [..] sub potenti manu Dei?, demütigt euch derhalb und [..]   ["Dei" = "Dej"?]
005.13 [..]d {struck: Gott?} Altem?/Alten? in einer angst?, {struck: last euch bieg?} bedt?/bedenckt?
005.14 [..]d? welcher sich biegt und brauch(en) lasst wo man ..
005.15 [..]st aber {struck: [..]} {struck: [..]} (interlinear: "aller"?) auss welche(m) Christus ein Ci[..]  [last word struck?]
005.16 [..]formiert? und in dem {struck: [..]} seiner allmacht mit
005.17 [..]ist? gebrennet? hat. Den {struck: der kein? bliendige? hat} (interlinear above struck words: "der ..."?)
005.18 [..]und sich ein {struck: [..]} jedliche form nach {struck: meinung d(er) ..}
005.19 {struck: [..] .. die demuth die unterwirfft sich jedman[..]}
005.20 [..]ond? die 4 Elementen d(er) unterist, (interlinear: "gleich") {struck: als} ein bestendige f[..]
005.21 [..] {struck: ..} {struck: als?} welche den ganz? last d(er) welt ert[..]
005.22 [cut at foot of tile; illegible]
Limitation: many cancellations overlap; struck/unstruck status of some words is unsure.

=== image-006 (centre tile of plate 001) ===
Left strip: right edge of Fragment A; only line-ends, all overlapping 005 (no new text beyond 1-2 letters):
 005.1 "..genommen"; 005.2 "..den Ale[..]" (struck); 005.3 "..[.]ich d(en) H[o..]"; 005.4 "..samblt"; 005.5 "..mit g[..]";
 005.6 "..Jungfr[..]"; interl. above 005.7 "..wie man [..]sse? in [..]"; 005.7 "..Proph[..]" (struck); 005.8 "..um? den";
 005.9 "..Wim[..]"; 005.10 "..effi[..]" (struck); 005.11 "..Reich" (struck? "d(as) Reich"); 005.12 "..und"; 005.13 "..bedt";
 005.14 "..man ..."; 005.15 "..Ci[..]" (struck); 005.16 "..mit"; 005.17 "..hat" (struck); 005.18 "..d(er) .."; 005.19 "..jedma[n]" (struck);
 005.20 "..bestendigh"; 005.21 "..ert[..]". The paper edge is straight: line-ends are cut by trimming.
Upper right: lower-left part of Fragment B (torn). Line beginnings (continuing 004):
 = 004.12 "Tityre"; 004.13 "Exordium"; 004.14 "Tityri et"
006.a  (smaller, interlinear/indented under 004.14) "[b]rimigs?"/"Primiges?" [uncertain, faint]
006.b  Sylvestre [..]   (continues in 007)
Bottom right corner: top edge of Fragment C (read on 009/010).

=== image-007 (middle-right tile of plate 001): lower part of Fragment B ===
Overlap: 007.1-3 = 004.12-14. The mark right of 004.14 is beyond the right ruled line: a looped sign like "3o"/"&"/flourish (darker ink).
007.1  Tityre tu? pa[..]? recubans sub tegmine fa[..]   (= 004.12; still faint, nothing more legible)
007.2  Exordium quod captat benevolentiam a persona   (= 004.13; "benevolentiam" faint, b- and -tiam visible)
007.3  Tityri et simul eu(m)? felicem praedicat.      (= 004.14; after "simul" a short word with macron, "eu(m)"/"illu(m)"?)
007.4  (interlinear, small, above "Sylvestre"): "brimigs? .. ..ng"? [illegible, possibly not Latin]
007.5  Sylvestre[m]? [..]enui? musam medit?[..]ris avena.   [after "Sylvestre" a word heavily faded/abraded: "tenui"? -- uncertain; "medi..ris" with a gap]
007.6  [torn start] [..]onia? [..] e? ostorale?/pastorale?   [very faint]
007.7  [torn, bottom edge cuts letters] .. [..]tatione? cuius? fu[..]?/fun[..]?
Fragment B lower edge is torn below this; lower-left corner lost.
Bottom left of tile: top lines of Fragment C (read on 010).

=== image-008 (bottom-left tile of plate 001): foot of Fragment A ===
Overlap: 008.1-4 = 005.18-21. A long diagonal stroke runs from upper right (c. 008.3) down-left across 008.4-6 (cancellation of a passage?).
008.1  [..]und sich ein {struck: [..]} jedliche form nach {struck: meinung d(er) ..}       (= 005.18)
008.2  {struck: [..]lche? ist ... die demuth die unterwirfft sich jedma[n]}             (= 005.19; interlinear "gleich" over next line)
008.3  [..]ond? die 4 Elementen d(er) unterist, (interl. "gleich") {struck: als} ein bestendige f[..]  (= 005.20)
008.4  [..] grundfest {struck: als} welche den ganz? last d(er) welt ertr[..]           (= 005.21; first word now "grundfest")
008.5  [..]ist ein grundfest und {struck: fundament [..]} aller? Dingen?/dinste?   [diagonal stroke crosses; "aller Dinge" uncertain]
008.6  [..]brennet? von dem Feuer, last es sich nit also b[..]
008.7  [..] bricht vil eher, Also ist warhafftig die [..]
008.8  (lower margin, larger script, underlined "infer.."): [pencil shelfmark "Stams, StA / Frg. 183_3r"] [flourished sign: "B"/"3" with long tail] . Et porta infer[..]
Foot edge torn; nothing below 008.8.

=== image-010 (bottom-right tile of plate 001): Fragment C, right part ===
Observation: Latin cursive, darker brown ink, single column, abbreviations (macrons, p-bar/pro, q-forms, -us sign "9"-like).
Line beginnings are cut by the trimmed left edge (see 009). A grey rectangle (modern masking card) lies over the plate
to the right of the paper's lower right; paper continues under it? -- the line-ends 010.4-12 reach the card's edge, so a few
letters may be hidden. Line numbers counted from the top of image-010.
010.1  [top line, cut by upper edge] [..]p? [..] .. [illegible]     [ascenders only, plus a tall looped letter mid-line]
010.2  [..]l(is)? supernaturalis. Naturalis e(st) q(uae)? d(i)c?um? et        [word after "q": "dcum"/"decem"? uncertain]
010.3  [..]q(ue) quotcu(m)q(ue)? lumine n(atura)li? et p(ro)priis
010.4  [..]unt cognosci, qualem etiam? potuerunt
010.5  [..] Supernaturalis est qua Deus? et res
